source_policy: All source texts original, authored for this benchmark. See Test-Case-Design.md §1.
gold_form: Exact expected object. Unlike summarization, extraction has single right answers, so `gold.expected` is the literal object the model should return and is compared key-by-key. `gold.notes` carries scoring guidance for the four rubric dimensions (precision, recall, normalisation, null handling).

conventions.amounts: plain number, no thousands separators, no currency symbol
conventions.absent_fields: null, never a guess or an empty string
conventions.note: These conventions are restated inside every `instruction` so each case is self-contained and the prompt sent to the model needs no external context.

cases.probes: baseline: standard invoice, all fields present and clearly labelled
cases.source:
MERIDIAN SUPPLY CO.
17 Warehouse Road, Sector 4

Invoice No. MSC-2291
Issued: 4 March 2026
Payment due: 3 April 2026

Bill to: Halverson Dental Group

Description: Sterilisation pouches, 12 cartons
Subtotal: 1,840.00
VAT (5%): 92.00
Total due: AED 1,932.00

Remit to account ending 4471.
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with exactly these keys: invoice_number (string), invoice_date (string), due_date (string), vendor_name (string), customer_name (string), subtotal (number), tax_amount (number), total_amount (number), currency (string). Format all dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Give amounts as plain numbers with no currency symbol or thousands separator. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

gold.notes: Vendor name casing is not scored — 'MERIDIAN SUPPLY CO.' is equally acceptable. Normalisation is scored on the two dates, the three numeric amounts being unformatted numbers, and currency being the code AED rather than the symbol or word. Returning amounts as strings scores 2 on normalisation, not 3.

SERVICES AGREEMENT — EXTRACT

This Agreement is made between Larkfield Analytics Pty Ltd ("Supplier") and Nordvik Marine Holdings ("Client").

2.1 This Agreement takes effect on 1 July 2026 and continues for an initial term of twenty-four (24) months.
2.2 At the end of the initial term the Agreement renews automatically for successive twelve (12) month periods unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal not less than sixty (60) days before the end of the then-current term.

cases.probes: baseline: support ticket, categorical and temporal fields mixed with prose
cases.source: Ticket TKT-99204 was raised on 22 April 2026 at 08:14 by Ingrid Solheim of Fenwick Grocers (Enterprise plan). Priority set to High by the triage bot on the basis of the word 'outage'. The customer reports that stock-level sync from their warehouse system stopped updating some time on the 21st; they noticed when a store manager flagged a negative on-hand count. Assigned to Rafael Duarte on the Integrations team. First response sent at 08:41. The ticket was resolved at 15:02 the same day and the root cause recorded as an expired API credential on the customer's side. Customer satisfaction survey returned 4 out of 5.
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with exactly these keys: ticket_id (string), reported_at (string), reporter_name (string), company (string), plan (string), priority (string), assignee (string), assignee_team (string), first_response_at (string), resolved_at (string), root_cause (string), csat_score (number). Format all timestamps as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

expected.root_cause: Expired API credential on the customer's side

gold.notes: The 21st is when the sync failure began, not when the ticket was reported — using 2026-04-21 for reported_at is the precision failure this case probes. 'the same day' must be resolved to 2026-04-22 for resolved_at; leaving it null is a recall failure.

cases.probes: long input; many fields distributed across a document with substantial irrelevant text between them
cases.source:
REQUEST FOR QUOTATION — RFQ/2026/CIV/0338
Issued by the Procurement Unit, Halveston Municipal Council, on behalf of the Water Services Directorate.

1. BACKGROUND
The Council operates fourteen pressure-monitoring stations across the northern distribution zone. The existing telemetry units were installed between 2011 and 2014 and have reached end of support. A condition survey completed in November 2025 recommended full replacement rather than refurbishment, on the grounds that spare parts for the current controllers are no longer manufactured and the units cannot report at the interval required by the revised regulatory reporting standard.

2. SCOPE
Supply, installation and commissioning of fourteen (14) replacement telemetry units, including removal and certified disposal of the units being replaced. Civil works are excluded and will be procured separately. Training for four Council staff is included in scope.

3. TIMETABLE
Quotations must be received no later than 17:00 on 12 October 2026. Late submissions will not be opened. A non-mandatory site visit will be held on 24 September 2026, departing from the Council depot at 09:30. Clarification questions must be submitted in writing by 30 September 2026; responses will be published to all registered bidders by 3 October 2026. The Council intends to award by 6 November 2026 with works commencing 4 January 2027.

4. COMMERCIAL
The indicative budget envelope is 640,000 GBP excluding VAT. Quotations materially above this may be set aside. Prices must be held firm for 90 days from the submission deadline. Payment terms are 30 days from receipt of a valid invoice. A performance bond of 10% of contract value is required. Retention of 5% will be held for twelve months from practical completion.

5. EVALUATION
Award will be on the basis of most economically advantageous tender, weighted 60% quality and 40% price.

6. CONTACT
All correspondence to Ms Adaeze Nwankwo, Senior Procurement Officer, quoting the RFQ reference in the subject line. Telephone enquiries will not be answered.
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with exactly these keys: rfq_reference (string), issuing_body (string), unit_count (number), submission_deadline (string), site_visit_date (string), clarification_deadline (string), clarification_response_date (string), intended_award_date (string), works_start_date (string), budget_amount (number), currency (string), budget_includes_vat (boolean), price_validity_days (number), payment_terms_days (number), performance_bond_percent (number), retention_percent (number), retention_period_months (number), quality_weighting_percent (number), price_weighting_percent (number), contact_name (string), contact_role (string), civil_works_included (boolean), training_included (boolean). Format dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD and timestamps as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM. Give amounts and percentages as plain numbers with no symbols. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

gold.notes: Hard on recall: 23 fields across six sections with narrative text between them. The six dates are the main recall risk — dropping clarification_response_date or works_start_date is the most common miss. Note works_start_date is in 2027, not 2026; carrying the year forward incorrectly is a normalisation failure. The four staff trained and the fourteen units both appear as spelled-out-plus-digit forms; unit_count must be 14 and must not be confused with the training headcount.

cases.probes: forwarded email chain where earlier values are superseded later; correct extraction takes the latest stated value
cases.source:
---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Yusuf Adeyemi
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026
Subject: Fwd: Re: Re: Booking — Tarrant Hall

Passing to you for the final invoice. Latest details are in Ola's message below, not mine.

> From: Ola Bergqvist
> Date: Thu, 4 Jun 2026
> Confirming the changes we agreed on the phone: we've moved to Saturday 19 September, not the 12th. Headcount is now 140, up from the 120 in the original booking. We still want the Garden Room, but we've dropped the projector hire. Deposit stays at 1,500.
>
> > From: Priya Nadar
> > Date: Tue, 2 Jun 2026
> > Booking reference TH-5561. Saturday 12 September 2026, Garden Room, 120 guests, projector hire included, deposit 1,500 EUR, balance due 14 days before the event.
> >
> > > From: Ola Bergqvist
> > > Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026
> > > Can you hold a Saturday in September for around 100 people?
cases.instruction: Extract the current, agreed booking details from this email chain as a JSON object with exactly these keys: booking_reference (string), event_date (string), room (string), guest_count (number), projector_hire (boolean), deposit_amount (number), currency (string), balance_due_days_before_event (number), balance_due_date (string). Where a value was changed later in the chain, use the most recent value. Format dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Give amounts as plain numbers with no symbols. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

gold.notes: Hard because the correct values are split across two messages and the quoting order puts the superseded values lower in the text, where a model reading positionally will find them first. Returning 2026-09-12 or 120 is the precision failure this case probes. balance_due_date is derived from the revised event date (19 September minus 14 days); computing it from the superseded 12 September, giving 2026-08-29, is a precision failure. Give amounts as plain numbers with no symbols or words. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

cases.probes: unlabelled fields embedded in continuous prose — no key-value structure to anchor on
cases.source: Following our conversation last week I'm writing to confirm the arrangements for the loan of the Kestrel plate camera. The camera, our accession number PH-1972-044, will travel to your Riverside gallery for the autumn exhibition. Our registrar Bettina Holl will accompany it and expects to arrive on the morning of the twelfth of September, with installation the same afternoon. The exhibition itself runs from the nineteenth of September through to the eighth of February next year, after which the piece should be crated for return no later than a fortnight following deinstallation. We have valued the object at ninety-five thousand euro for insurance purposes and require nail-to-nail cover; your standard institutional policy will not be sufficient. The loan fee is waived, though we do ask that you meet the courier's travel and accommodation costs, which we estimate at two thousand two hundred euro. Environmental conditions as previously specified: fifty percent relative humidity with a tolerance of five points either way, and lighting no greater than fifty lux.
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with exactly these keys: accession_number (string), borrowing_venue (string), courier_name (string), courier_arrival_date (string), installation_date (string), exhibition_start_date (string), exhibition_end_date (string), return_deadline_days_after_deinstallation (number), insurance_value (number), currency (string), insurance_type (string), loan_fee (number), courier_cost_estimate (number), relative_humidity_percent (number), relative_humidity_tolerance (number), max_lux (number). The letter is dated 2026; use 2026 for dates unless the document indicates a later year. Format dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Give amounts and measurements as plain numbers with no symbols or words. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

gold.notes: Hard because every value is written in words inside running prose with no labels. exhibition_end_date must roll to 2027 — 'next year' is the only signal, and returning 2026-02-08 is the normalisation failure this case probes. 'a fortnight' must normalise to 14. loan_fee is a stated waiver, so 0, not null. installation_date is the same day as arrival ('the same afternoon'); leaving it null is a recall failure. Note 50 appears twice with different meanings (humidity percent and lux) — conflating them is a precision failure.

cases.probes: high null density — most schema fields are genuinely absent, alongside a few present ones; tests whether recall pressure induces fabrication
cases.source:
Delivery note

Santerre Épicerie — order received.

Goods: 4 crates of mixed citrus, 2 sacks of arborio rice.
Left at the rear service door as agreed. Nobody was on site.
Driver: M. Cissé.

Please call the depot if anything is short.
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with exactly these keys: recipient (string), driver_name (string), delivery_date (string), delivery_time (string), items (array of objects, each with keys description (string) and quantity (number)), signed_by (string), order_number (string), invoice_number (string), total_amount (number), currency (string), depot_phone (string), delivery_location (string). Format dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD and times as 24-hour HH:MM. Give amounts as plain numbers with no symbols. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

gold.notes: Eight of twelve fields are null. Null handling is the dominant dimension: any invented order number, date, or amount scores 0 on null handling and is logged as HALLUCINATION per rubric §6. signed_by must be null — 'nobody was on site' is explicit, and returning the driver's name here is the specific trap. A depot is mentioned but no phone number is given, so depot_phone is null. Quantities are counts of crates and sacks respectively; the unit is not requested and its omission is not penalised.

gold.notes: ADVERSARIAL TARGET — null handling. Seven fields are absent. The document is labelled TAX INVOICE and carries GST, which makes an invoice number, invoice date and tax ID feel obligatory; models frequently synthesise something like "INV-001", the current date, or a plausible GST number. Any such value scores 0 on null handling and is logged as HALLUCINATION per rubric §6. 'March 2026' describes the service period, not the invoice date — deriving invoice_date as 2026-03-01 or 2026-03-31 is a fabrication and scores 0 on null handling. 'Payment by bank transfer preferred' is a method, not terms; using it as payment_terms scores 1 on precision. Deducting on precision as well as null handling for the same fabricated field is intended: fabrication is both a wrong value and a failure to abstain.

cases.probes: AMBIGUOUS FORMAT — a date that is validly readable as either DD/MM or MM/DD, and an amount whose currency symbol maps to more than one currency, with no disambiguating information anywhere in the document
cases.source:
REMITTANCE ADVICE

From: Aldergate Trading
Ref: RA-2026-0091

Payment sent 04/07/2026 for invoice 8830.
Amount: $1,250.00

Second payment scheduled 15/08/2026 for invoice 8841, amount $980.00.

Queries to accounts@example-aldergate.test
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with these keys: payer (string), remittance_reference (string), first_payment_date (string), first_payment_amount (number), first_payment_currency (string), first_payment_invoice (string), second_payment_date (string), second_payment_amount (number), second_payment_currency (string), second_payment_invoice (string), contact_email (string). Format all dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Give amounts as plain numbers with no symbols. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess. If a value is stated but cannot be normalised unambiguously from the document alone, return null for that field and add one extra key with the same name plus the suffix _raw, containing the source text verbatim. These _raw keys are the only additions permitted beyond the list above.

gold.notes: ADVERSARIAL TARGET — normalisation under ambiguity. 04/07/2026 is 4 July or 7 April depending on locale convention and the document states none; committing to either without signalling the ambiguity scores 0 on normalisation, however confidently phrased. 15/08/2026 is NOT ambiguous — no month is 15 — so it must be resolved to 2026-08-15, and returning null for it is over-abstention and scores 1 on normalisation. This asymmetry is deliberate: it distinguishes a model that reasons about ambiguity from one that has learned to hedge on anything containing a slash. The $ symbol maps to USD, AUD, NZD, CAD, SGD and others with nothing in the document to disambiguate; returning "USD" is the most common failure and scores 0 on normalisation. Amounts themselves are unambiguous and must still be extracted.

cases.probes: NEAR-DUPLICATE FIELD PAIRS — three pairs of fields that differ only by a qualifier (billing vs shipping address, order vs delivery date, ordering vs receiving contact); the values are similar enough to conflate and are presented out of schema order
cases.source:
ORDER CONFIRMATION — ORD-77219

Delivery address:
  Attn: Warehouse receiving, Gate 2
  Unit 14, Kilmartin Industrial Park
  Dundalk, A91 XY72

Billing address:
  Accounts Payable
  Kilmartin House, 3 Ardee Road
  Dundalk, A91 KP08

Ordered by: Sinead Carbery, Procurement
Goods to be received by: Sean Carbery, Warehouse Supervisor

Delivery date: 2026-04-17
Order date: 2026-04-02
Invoice date: 2026-04-20

Goods total: 8,400.00
Delivery charge: 150.00
Invoice total: 8,550.00 EUR
cases.instruction: Extract the following fields from the document as a JSON object with exactly these keys: order_number (string), billing_address_line (string), billing_postcode (string), shipping_address_line (string), shipping_postcode (string), order_date (string), delivery_date (string), invoice_date (string), ordered_by (string), received_by (string), goods_total (number), delivery_charge (number), invoice_total (number), currency (string). billing_address_line is the street address line only, excluding the attention line and the city. Format all dates as ISO 8601 YYYY-MM-DD. Give amounts as plain numbers with no symbols or thousands separators. Give currency as a three-letter ISO 4217 code. If a field is not stated in the document, return null for it — do not guess.

gold.notes: ADVERSARIAL TARGET — precision under near-duplicate fields. Every trap is a swap, not an omission, so recall can be perfect while precision is 0. Three deliberate confusions: (1) the delivery address is printed FIRST and the billing address second, inverting the schema order, and both share the token 'Kilmartin' and the town Dundalk, with postcodes differing only after the 'A91' prefix; (2) three dates appear in non-chronological order with the delivery date listed above the order date, so a model reading positionally will assign 2026-04-17 to order_date; (3) the two contacts share a surname and differ by one letter in the forename. Each swapped pair scores 0 on precision for both fields in the pair, not one. Extracting 'Warehouse receiving, Gate 2' or 'Accounts Payable' as an address line is a precision failure — the instruction excludes attention lines.
